guidelineReference: SJA First Aid / minor wound care
title: Minor graze at a park event
setting: Park event. 58F fainted briefly, now alert, with a small graze on her arm from falling off a bicycle at low speed. Walking and talking normally.
verdictExplanation: Alert, fully responsive. However, unexplained exertional syncope in a patient with a cardiac history is a major clinical red flag for life-threatening arrhythmias or ischemia. Sick: requires an emergency ambulance.

shared.circulation: Minor graze on left forearm, slight bleeding

history.history: Slipped off bike on a gravel path moments ago, fainted briefly but recovered immediately
history.drugs: GTN spray (has not needed to use it today)
history.additional: Had a minor heart attack a year ago but currently completely pain-free and well

followUp.question: What is the most concerning clinical red flag in this patient's presentation?

options.text: The unexplained exertional syncope (fainting) while cycling
The minor superficial graze on her left forearm
The fact she is walking and talking normally

followUp.explanation: Exertional syncope (fainting during exercise) in a patient with a known cardiac history is a major clinical red flag for serious conditions like arrhythmias or ischemia. It mandates an immediate 999 call, even if the patient appears fully recovered and well.

evolving.narrative: While waiting for the ambulance, the patient suddenly clutches her chest, complains of severe central chest pain, and becomes pale and sweaty.
While waiting for the ambulance, the patient suddenly clutches her chest, complains of severe central chest pain radiating to her jaw, and becomes visibly pale and diaphoretic.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Clean and dress the graze. Recognize the red flag of exertional syncope. Prepare for sudden deterioration and potential cardiac arrest.
levelFlags.erNotes: Reassure and monitor. Recognize exertional syncope as a red flag. Anticipate cardiac chest pain and have the AED ready.
